lineupSource: Yahoo Sport UK / Roundtable projected XI, 20 August 2026, cross-checked on 21 August against Fantasy Football Scout's Friday predicted line-ups and Chelsea's own report of Xabi Alonso's 20 August press conference, re-checked on 22 August against Goal's 21 August preview, the Evening Standard / Yahoo Chelsea XI piece of 20 August, Sports Mole's 21 August injury and suspension list and The Pride of London's predicted XI, and re-checked again on 23 August against Rotowire's 22 August predicted line-ups, Sports Illustrated's 23 August Chelsea predicted XI, Football365's 23 August match preview and Sky Sports' 23 August team-news page. Still a projection, not team news — Sky confirmed on 23 August that no official sheet exists for either side, and none will until roughly an hour before Monday's 20:00 BST kickoff.
lineupNote: Still a projection, and Friday's crop of previews widened the spread rather than narrowing it. This 3-4-2-1 remains the modal call — Yahoo Sport and Roundtable both keep Reece James in a back three with Pedro Neto and Marco Palestra as the wing-backs — but Goal's 21 August preview keeps the same back three and reads the front as a 3-4-3 — João Pedro flanked by Palmer and Morgan Rogers rather than playing off a lone striker — with Romeo Lavia in the midfield two ahead of Enzo Fernández; the Evening Standard goes to a 4-3-3 with Jorrel Hato at left-back and James at right-back; and The Pride of London keeps James at right wing-back and promotes Josh Acheampong into the back three alongside Colwill and Lacroix. Four previews, four different answers on the back three, which with the left wing-back slot remains the least settled call here. Wesley Fofana is suspended, a ban carried over from his final-day red card at Sunderland that pre-season friendlies do not clear, and that is what pushes James from midfield into the back three. How long that ban runs is genuinely unclear: it has been reported as a single match, but the Sunderland dismissal was his second two-yellow red of 2025-26 after the one against Burnley, and at least one outlet has him banned for Alonso's first two games — Fulham and Brighton. No mainstream preview commits to a length, and none of it changes Monday: he is out at Craven Cottage either way. Enzo Fernández is staying — Alonso said flatly that Enzo is a Chelsea player once Manchester City let Chelsea's 14 August bid deadline pass — and is expected to feature. Palestra, the £43m signing from Atalanta and Serie A Defender of the Year after 37 loan appearances at Cagliari, can play either flank, so the left wing-back call still turns on whether Alonso wants his attacking edge there ahead of Hato or of Pep Chavarría, the £16.3m arrival from Rayo Vallecano signed to replace Marc Cucurella. The absence list hardened since Thursday: Goal now lists Caleb Wiley, Jordan Henderson, Aaron Anselmino, Mamadou Sarr, Emanuel Emegha and Geovany Quenda as ruled out, though the Standard the same day still files Henderson (wrist) and Emegha (hamstring) as doubts rather than definite absentees. Alonso reported no fresh injury concerns and said Danny Welbeck, managed through a minor problem, returns to team training on Saturday and can be involved. The standing caveat is unchanged: James, Fernández, Maxence Lacroix and Morgan Rogers all reported back late from the World Cup and are selectable but may be eased in, so any of the four could start on the bench.

lineupNote: A guess, and a lower-confidence one than usual: this is a rotation night, and rotation is the hardest thing to predict. Three previews produced three different shapes — Sports Mole a 4-2-3-1, Sports Illustrated a 3-4-2-1, 101 Great Goals a 4-3-3 — and only seven names appear in all three (Penders, Acheampong, Lacroix, Chavarría, Barco, Estêvão, Welbeck). Sports Mole's XI is used here because its availability list is the only one that squares with what Alonso actually said on Wednesday. Alonso has signalled wholesale changes, so first Chelsea starts are in play for Danny Welbeck, Valentín Barco, Pep Chavarría and goalkeeper Mike Penders, with Penders getting the kind of look that decides whether he pushes Robert Sánchez. Two source conflicts are worth stating plainly rather than smoothing over. First, Wesley Fofana: Sports Mole has him serving the second match of a two-game ban and therefore out tonight, while Sports Illustrated and 101 Great Goals both start him. The two-game reading is the better-supported one and is what this site has used for Sunday's Brighton page — a red-card ban runs across domestic competitions, so the opener plus this tie discharges it and he is clear for Brighton, not for Luton. He is left out here on that basis, but it is a genuine disagreement, not a settled fact. Second, 101 Great Goals starts Marco Palestra, which looks stale: Alonso ruled Palestra out on Wednesday alongside Moisés Caicedo, and was notably less hopeful about Palestra — “Both not for tomorrow. Hopefully Moi can make it for the weekend. Maybe we need to check a little bit more with Marco.” Cole Palmer is not injured; he is expected to be rested with Sunday in mind. Jordan Henderson (wrist) is out and targeting 6 September at Arsenal, Emanuel Emegha's status is reported inconsistently — Sports Mole has him fit and available, 101 Great Goals still lists a hamstring problem — and Aaron Anselmino (hamstring) is a doubt. Enzo Fernández is fit and expected to be involved in some capacity, though Manchester City interest and a 1 September window deadline make him the one selection Alonso may be managing for non-football reasons. Geovany Quenda's key stat is deliberately blank: he moved from Sporting CP this summer and the public 2025-26 numbers for him conflict badly across sources, so nothing is stated rather than guessed.
notes: Xabi Alonso's first competitive home match as Chelsea manager. Luton are a League One side managed by former Arsenal midfielder Jack Wilshere, and arrive having won the EFL Trophy last season. Alonso's Wednesday press conference ruled out Caicedo and Palestra for this tie. Expect heavy rotation. The third-round draw was made on Wednesday evening, before this tie is played: the winner goes away to Leeds United, in the weeks beginning 7 or 14 September.

Alonso's first home game in charge. The rescheduling question is settled: the Premier League's August-September fixture-amendment notice confirms this as Sunday 30 August, 14:00 BST, moved to accommodate Brighton's UEFA Conference League playoff tie the preceding Thursday. Chelsea also had an EFL Cup tie against Luton on Thursday 27 August, three days before this one, so rotation is a live factor. Brighton arrive short of forwards: Yankuba Minteh (leg) is out for several weeks, Evan Ferguson (ankle) is not expected back until late October or November, Stefanos Tzimas (knee) is targeted for early-to-mid October, and Kaoru Mitoma is still working back from summer hamstring surgery — Hürzeler says he is getting closer but he is not available here. Jack Hinshelwood picked up a training injury and Hürzeler called the weekend likely too soon for him. Georginio Rutter has been in a protective boot since the Aston Villa fixture and faces a late fitness test; he is the more likely of the two to feature but is now a genuine doubt rather than a probable. New signings Promise David and Jaouen Hadjam are expected to be options, and Pascal Struijk and Ferdi Kadioğlu are back in the squad. The practical read: Brighton are missing four of their forward options and may be without a fifth, so Chelsea's back three should face a less direct attacking threat than Brighton's league position suggests.

lineupNote: Seven changes, and the projection could not have caught the biggest one: Chelsea announced the signing of Emiliano Martínez from Aston Villa for about £7.5m on Sunday morning and he went straight into goal. Robert Sánchez was left out of the squad entirely and Mike Penders dropped to the bench. Enzo Fernández was also omitted amid Manchester City interest. Alonso reverted to a back three after using 4-2-3-1 against Luton, with Fofana back from suspension alongside Lacroix and Colwill. Neto, Lavia and Hato all returned, Malo Gusto was pushed into midfield, and Reece James was rested. Substitutes: Penders, Acheampong, Chavarría, James, Barco, Caicedo, Estêvão, Gittens, Welbeck.

notes: Alonso's first competitive meeting with childhood friend Mikel Arteta as a fellow manager. Arsenal are the reigning champions. This is Chelsea's first match since the summer transfer window shut on Tuesday 1 September, and it closed with two departures that change the team. Enzo Fernandez has gone to Manchester City for GBP 125m on a five-year deal, a British-record-equalling fee and a reunion with Enzo Maresca; Chelsea booked roughly an GBP 18m profit on the fee they paid Benfica three and a half years ago. Chelsea had lined up Monaco's Lamine Camara as the replacement and that deal collapsed late on deadline day, so there is no direct like-for-like signing to slot in; Alonso's public line on Friday was that he is 'prepared and happy with the squad and the depth we have'. Goalkeeper Robert Sanchez also left, joining Cesc Fabregas's Como on a season-long loan, which leaves Emiliano Martinez and Mike Penders as the senior keepers. Marc Guiu moved to RB Leipzig. BOTH PRESS CONFERENCES HAVE NOW HAPPENED, at 1:30pm UK on Friday 4 September, and the picture they leave is meaningfully different from what this page said on Thursday night - in both directions. CHELSEA: Moises Caicedo is NOT ruled out. Alonso deliberately gave nothing away, saying only 'We will check tomorrow. Tomorrow is the last decision for the squad on Sunday', and when pressed added 'we need to not worry about these things that happen and we need to check tomorrow and take a final decision'. That is softer than Thursday's reporting, which had him very unlikely to feature. Treat him as a genuine Saturday call rather than an absentee. Jordan Henderson has been upgraded: after wrist surgery Alonso now says he is 'getting closer and closer to playing time', which is ahead of the mid-September return the injury trackers had projected. Alonso talked through the midfield options he does have, naming Valentin Barco ('young but he has come with great energy'), Henderson ('the composure, the mentality'), Reece James, Malo Gusto and academy midfielder Reggie Watson. On managing Romeo Lavia and James he said 'hopefully, touch wood, they don't have that many setbacks'. Emmanuel Emegha is back from the injury that cost him pre-season. Marco Palestra did not come up at all, so he stays an unknown. ARSENAL: their situation has improved, and the 'thin and unsettled' framing this page carried on Thursday no longer holds - be candid that it was overtaken within a day. Declan Rice is fit and available; he trained on Thursday and the knock he picked up against Aston Villa has cleared. Bruno Guimaraes, the GBP 75m arrival from Newcastle, missed Thursday's session but Arteta expects him back, saying he would 'probably tomorrow be OK to train', and he is expected to be involved. Cristhian Mosquera is the one genuine doubt left: he has not trained since a strain Arteta describes as precautionary and is due to test it on Saturday, with Ezri Konsa, a GBP 51m summer signing from Aston Villa, in line for his first competitive Arsenal start alongside Gabriel if Mosquera does not make it. Riccardo Calafiori is fit and was nominated for Premier League Player of the Month. Jurrien Timber is close, with Arteta saying he is 'in really good condition', but this is likely too soon after a groin problem and the bench is realistically his ceiling. William Saliba remains out with a back injury and is months rather than weeks away. MARKET: the line has drifted slightly Chelsea's way. DraftKings now price Chelsea +380, in from +425 on Thursday, with Arsenal -155 and the draw +260 both unmoved - so the move is real but small, and Arsenal are still a clear favourite at a de-vigged 56 percent. Chelsea then host Leeds United in the Carabao Cup third round on the Wednesday, three days after this, so squad management is again in play. FRIDAY EVENING UPDATE. Nothing official has changed since the morning - Caicedo is still a Saturday call and Mosquera still has a Saturday fitness test - but the day's previews sharpened three things. First, the Chelsea midfield projection on this page has moved: the consensus is now Reece James alongside Lavia rather than Malo Gusto, with Sports Mole the lone dissenter putting James at right wing-back instead. Second, Alonso's own framing of the Caicedo problem is more hopeful than Thursday's reporting suggested - his words were that hopefully it is not new and it was not more than last time - while Henderson is described as waiting on the green light for his debut after wrist surgery and Palestra still has no return date. Third, on the Arsenal side Mosquera's problem is now being reported specifically as a hamstring scare, with Ezri Konsa in line to start alongside Gabriel, and there is a genuine split over Arsenal's second midfielder: NBC Sports projects Myles Lewis-Skelly next to Declan Rice, while Yahoo Sport and Sports Mole expect Bruno Guimaraes to be fit enough to start. Christos Tzolis is expected on the left but Eberechi Eze is competition for that shirt. One forward-looking note worth having in front of you: Cole Palmer is one goal away from 50 Premier League goals for Chelsea, which he would reach inside 100 appearances - a club record pace. Odds, kickoff and channel were all re-verified on Friday evening and none of them moved: DraftKings still have Arsenal -155, the draw +260 and Chelsea +380, and it is 10:30am Central on USA Network with Telemundo carrying the Spanish call. SATURDAY 5 SEPTEMBER UPDATE (morning Central). The Caicedo decision has still not been made public, and by Alonso's own timetable it will not be until later today - the final session at Cobham is under way as this is written and the squad is picked off the back of it. So nothing has actually resolved overnight: he remains a genuine doubt rather than an absentee, and the XI projected here still assumes he does not start. If he is passed fit he starts, and the midfield reshapes around him in a way none of the published projections capture. Two things did move. First, the market: DraftKings now price Chelsea +370, in from +380 on Friday and +425 on Thursday, while Arsenal -155 and the draw +260 have now held through three straight checks. So the drift is consistently one-way and consistently small - Chelsea are being backed, but the de-vigged read is still only 20 percent Chelsea, 25 percent draw, 55 percent Arsenal, and Arsenal remain a clear favourite. Second, Arsenal's midfield question has largely resolved: Friday's split between Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes has tipped, and the previews checked this morning now converge on Guimaraes starting alongside Declan Rice. Cristhian Mosquera's hamstring scare has not cleared, so Ezri Konsa is expected in alongside Gabriel for his first competitive Arsenal start. The rest of the expected Arsenal shape is Raya in goal, White and Calafiori at full-back, and Saka, Odegaard and Christos Tzolis behind Kai Havertz, with Saliba and Timber both unavailable. Kickoff and channel were re-checked this morning and are unchanged for a third time: 16:30 UK, 10:30am Central, USA Network. One caution worth recording, because it nearly caused an error here: a prominent Sports Illustrated headline reading 'triple Chelsea fitness update for Arsenal tie as Caicedo ruled out' is a January 2026 article about an entirely different two-legged cup fixture under a different head coach, in which Caicedo was suspended rather than injured. It has nothing to do with Sunday and was discarded. That is the second stale-source trap on this fixture in two days. SATURDAY 5 SEPTEMBER, EVENING UPDATE (6pm Central, which is just past midnight in London). Caicedo has still not been resolved publicly, and Alonso's own timetable has now run out. The final Cobham session happened during the day and the squad has been picked off the back of it, but nothing has been published and Chelsea have not put out a squad list. Realistically that means the answer now arrives with the team sheet about an hour before kickoff rather than tonight, and the automated official-XI checks are armed for 9:35am and 9:50am Central on Sunday to catch it. The XI projected here still assumes he does not start. The most precise public framing remains the club's own: Alonso has said Caicedo could be fit enough to feature from the bench, which makes the bench his realistic ceiling rather than a start - but it is still not a ruling-out, and it is a better position than Thursday's reporting implied. MARKET: the DraftKings line was re-checked at 6pm Central and is unchanged for a fourth consecutive check - Arsenal -155, the draw +260, Chelsea +370, de-vigging to 20 percent Chelsea, 25 percent draw, 55 percent Arsenal. The one-way drift toward Chelsea earlier in the week has stopped. A market caution worth recording: a DraftKings Network prediction column published on 5 September quotes Arsenal -145, the draw +265 and Chelsea +425. Those are not the live board and they are not internally consistent - Chelsea +425 was Thursday's number, from before the drift - so they read as an opening-line snapshot carried into a column drafted earlier. ESPN's live DraftKings feed is what this page uses and it reads -155 / +260 / +370. Kickoff and channel were re-verified for a fourth time and are unchanged: 16:30 UK, 11:30am Eastern, 10:30am Central, USA Network with Telemundo carrying the Spanish call. One genuine change in the preview landscape: the right wing-back slot, a two-way argument on Friday, is now a three-way one. Premier League News Now, publishing under a 6 September dateline, puts Malo Gusto there for defensive stability with Pedro Neto dropping out, which sits alongside Sports Mole's version that puts Reece James on that flank. Against that, the previews are now close to unanimous that James starts in central midfield alongside Lavia. So the settled part of this projection has got more settled and the unsettled part has got messier. Finally, for a fourth straight day the Sports Illustrated headline reading 'triple Chelsea fitness update for Arsenal tie as Caicedo ruled out' is still surfacing at the top of searches. It is still a January 2026 article about a different competition under a different head coach, and it was checked and discarded again rather than allowed to override Alonso's actual words. SUNDAY 6 SEPTEMBER - MATCHDAY MORNING UPDATE (8:00am Central, two and a half hours before kickoff). Moises Caicedo is still unresolved in public. Chelsea have not published a squad list, the club's own team-news article on chelseafc.com still carries only Alonso's Friday line that the decision would be taken on Saturday, and nothing has been added to it since. So the answer now arrives with the team sheet at about 9:30am Central, an hour before kickoff, and the automated official-XI checks are armed for 9:35am and 9:50am Central to capture it. The eleven projected here still assumes he does not start, and the club's own framing - that he could be fit enough to feature from the bench - remains the realistic ceiling rather than a start. MARKET, AND THIS IS THE ONE THING WORTH READING PROPERLY TODAY. The DraftKings board has moved for the first time in four checks: Arsenal are now -140 from -155, the draw +285 from +260, and Chelsea +390 from +370. At a glance that reads as Arsenal shortening and Chelsea drifting, and it is neither. All three prices got longer at the same time, which is not a view about the match - it is the book cutting its margin as kickoff approaches. The overround has fallen from about 9.9 percent to about 4.7 percent. Strip the vig out and the underlying read is almost exactly where it has sat all week: 19 percent Chelsea, 25 percent draw, 56 percent Arsenal, against 20/25/55 yesterday. The honest conclusion is that the market has not changed its mind about this match in four days, it has only got more efficient about pricing it - so do not read the bigger Chelsea number as pessimism. Chelsea are a 19 percent shot and Arsenal remain a clear favourite. That de-vigged read is independently corroborated by a Covers piece carrying DraftKings' own model percentages, which have Arsenal at 57. A CORRECTION TO THIS PAGE. This page said on Friday that Emmanuel Emegha is back from the injury that cost him pre-season. That was too strong. He did make the bench for the Carabao Cup tie, but Chelsea's own team-news article for this fixture treats him as still short of availability for the trip, with Alonso saying only that he had an injury and missed a lot of pre-season and that young players need to be patient. Treat him as building back, not available. Kickoff and channel were re-verified for a fifth time and are unchanged: 16:30 UK, 10:30am Central, USA Network, with Telemundo carrying the Spanish call. STALE-SOURCE WATCH, day five. The January 2026 Sports Illustrated 'Caicedo ruled out' story has finally stopped leading the results. Two match reports from a previous Chelsea-Arsenal meeting in December 2025 surfaced in its place and were identified and discarded; their headlines carry details of that match and are deliberately not recorded on this page.

reportTeamNews:
**Moisés Caicedo is out entirely** — not in the eleven and not among the nine substitutes. After five days of this page recording him as unresolved, the doubt Alonso would not close on Friday resolves the pessimistic way. The club had framed him at best as *could feature from the bench*.

**Levi Colwill drops to the bench.** Read it as minutes management rather than anything ominous: he is barely a year out from an ACL injury, Alonso has been explicit about handling his load, and he is available if needed.
reportChanges:
**Ten of the eleven projected here were right.** Two changes from matchweek 2, both straight swaps into the same 3-4-2-1.

The midfield projection holds: **Reece James alongside Romeo Lavia**, with James wearing the armband. The near-unanimous Sunday preview consensus was right about that.

**The one thing nobody saw coming is at the back.** Josh Acheampong starts in the back three — a change no published projection had, including this one. Every single one had Colwill starting. Acheampong, still 20 and a Cobham graduate, gets a London derby start at the Emirates on merit.
reportTactical: Acheampong's arrival shuffles the two who stay: **Wesley Fofana moves from the right of the three into the middle**, and **Maxence Lacroix from the middle to the right**. The shape is unchanged; the personnel inside it are not.
reportWatch:
Whether James can hold a central midfield role for ninety minutes against Arsenal's press — availability, not ability, has always been the question with him.

How a 20-year-old handles his first London derby start away from home, and whether Colwill is called on from the bench if it goes badly.

lineupNote: Still a guess, not a team sheet - and the 8 September check has made one part of it distinctly shakier. READ THIS FIRST: Cole Palmer is fit. Alonso's own words are that Palmer is absolutely fine, and two of the three published projections now start him. The XI listed here does not, so treat Palmer's absence from it as the single least reliable thing on this page. What all three outlets agree on is the spine, and that is worth trusting: Penders in goal, Lacroix and Colwill together, Chavarría on the left, Barco and Lavia in midfield, Welbeck up top - seven names, three sources, no disagreement. Everything forward of that is contested. This file lists Gusto, Quenda, Estêvão and Gittens in a 4-2-3-1; Sports Mole goes to a back three with Josh Acheampong and keeps Palmer; the Evening Standard also goes to a back three, with Wesley Fofana, Pedro Neto and Morgan Rogers alongside Palmer. We have deliberately left the recorded XI as one outlet's actual published lineup rather than stitching a hybrid out of three, because a blended XI nobody printed would read as more authoritative than it is. So: right shape and spine, genuinely unresolved attack, and a fair chance Palmer starts. Two further caveats - Colwill's inclusion assumes a returning ACL case is trusted with a start, and he was held out of the Arsenal trip with a slight fitness concern, so he is probable rather than certain; and no club team sheet exists for this tie until roughly an hour before kick-off.
notes: An all-Premier League tie at Stamford Bridge, Chelsea's third home match in under three weeks. Leeds are managed by Daniel Farke and are back in the third round for the first time since 2022/23. They arrive unbeaten in all competitions this season, so this is not the soft home draw the seeding makes it look like. Date and kick-off are confirmed by Chelsea: Wednesday 9 September, 8pm UK, which is 2pm Central. UK coverage is Sky Sports Main Event. For US viewers the important point is that this is NOT an NBC competition - CBS and Paramount Plus hold the American rights to the Carabao Cup, and Paramount Plus streams the large majority of ties in every round, which is also where the second-round tie was carried. The per-match US listing is still unpublished, so treat the platform as reliable and a specific channel number as unconfirmed. ODDS NOW POSTED (checked Sunday 6 September, evening). Pinnacle, William Hill, bwin and 1xBet are all quoted within a few cents of that, and an 18-book average of 1.63 / 4.00 / 4.71 sits on top of the same numbers. A PROJECTED XI IS NOW POSTED (checked Monday 7 September), superseding the 5 and 6 September checks, which found nothing usable - those searches returned only the April 2026 FA Cup semi-final between these same two clubs, a Wembley tie under a different manager with a squad list that no longer applies, so nothing from them was carried across. What changed is that real same-day reporting appeared: a Read Chelsea predicted XI dated 7 September, reading Penders; Gusto, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Barco, Lavia; Quenda, Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck. Treat it as a media projection and nothing more - Alonso's press conference for this tie is not until Tuesday 8 September, so the club has confirmed nothing, and the projection is recorded here as a guess rather than as team news. THE 7 SEPTEMBER EVENING RE-CHECK ADDED A SECOND, INDEPENDENT PROJECTION, which is the most useful new thing in this update. Sports Mole published its own predicted XI the same day and it agrees with Read Chelsea on nine of the eleven names: Penders; Lacroix and Colwill; Gusto and Chavarria; Barco and Lavia; Estevao; Welbeck. It differs on exactly two slots - Sports Mole starts Josh Acheampong in a back three and keeps Cole Palmer in the side, where this file has Quenda and Gittens. Nine of eleven from two outlets that did not copy each other is about as much confidence as a pre-presser projection can earn, so the shape and the spine are reasonably safe and those two slots are the ones to hold loosely. We kept Quenda and Gittens on the reasoning that heavy rotation is the stated expectation across the board and resting Palmer fits that better than starting him, but that is our judgement call, not a sourced fact, and it is the single most likely place this projection is wrong. A third piece the same day framed it as eight changes rather than nine, which points the same way regardless. AVAILABILITY, which is the firmer part of this: Moises Caicedo was not passed fit for the Arsenal trip and Alonso has said he was brought back too early from his injury, so he is not expected here, with the Hull game on Saturday 12 September the stated target instead. Alonso has since added that he does not want to make the same mistake twice with him, which is manager-speak for a cautious return rather than a quick one. Jordan Henderson is still waiting on his Chelsea debut with a wrist injury carried out of the World Cup, though there is a genuinely encouraging update: he was pictured in first-team training on 4 September and is described as getting closer to playing time. Reporting still frames his return as later in September rather than this tie, so do not expect him on Wednesday. Marco Palestra has DOWNGRADED since the morning check. This file previously said this tie was the earliest he could feature; the evening re-check supersedes that. He has not been available for any of Chelsea's four matches so far, has not been pictured in training for some time after a training-ground knock, and is now reported as unlikely for Wednesday, with Hull on 12 September the target for him too. Levi Colwill travelled with the squad to Arsenal without featuring, which is the main reason reporters have him coming straight into the back line. The scheduling context still does most of the work: this falls three days after the Arsenal away trip and four days before Hull at home, and Alonso rotated heavily in the second round, so a much-changed side is the expectation rather than the surprise. ONE SOURCING TRAP WORTH LOGGING: a Sports Illustrated piece headlined as confirmed third-round team news against Lincoln City surfaced high in the results and is last season's third round, not this one. It was discarded. Verify the season and publication date on anything that looks like a confirmed team sheet before it goes near this file. THE 8 SEPTEMBER CHECK ADDED A THIRD PROJECTION AND ONE PIECE OF REAL TEAM NEWS. The team news first, because it matters more: COLE PALMER IS FIT. Alonso's line is that Palmer is absolutely fine. That directly undercuts the judgement call logged here on 7 September, when we kept Quenda and Gittens and rested Palmer on the reasoning that heavy rotation made resting him likelier. Two of the three projections now in hand start him, so the recorded XI is probably wrong on that specific point and the lineupNote has been rewritten to say so up front rather than leaving it buried. The recorded XI itself has NOT been changed, and that is a considered decision: it is one outlet's actual published lineup, and blending three disagreeing projections into a hybrid nobody printed would make a guess look like a team sheet. Better to publish one real projection and flag honestly where it is weak. The third projection is from the Evening Standard, dated 8 September and read via Yahoo, and it reads Penders; Fofana, Lacroix, Colwill; Neto, Barco, Lavia, Chavarria; Rogers, Palmer; Welbeck - a 3-4-2-1. Set against the other two, the picture is now: seven names agreed by all three sources (Penders, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria, Barco, Lavia, Welbeck), two of three going to a back three rather than a flat four, and two of three starting Palmer. The spine is close to safe, the attack is genuinely unresolved. ONE MORE AVAILABILITY DETAIL: Colwill was kept out of the Arsenal trip with a slight fitness concern and is reported as able to feature on Wednesday, which is a small downgrade in certainty from the 7 September reading that had him coming straight in. The Caicedo, Henderson and Palestra positions are unchanged from the evening of 7 September - Caicedo is now being openly targeted at Hull on 12 September rather than this tie, Henderson is still waiting on a green light after the World Cup wrist injury, and Palestra remains unlikely with Hull his target too. This is the traditional Saturday 3pm UK slot, which means it is blacked out on UK television, but American viewers get it on linear TV: NBC Sports lists the fixture as 10am ET on USA Network, which is 9am Central. That listing comes from NBC's own published matchweek schedule rather than a third-party guide, and it agrees with the 3pm UK time quoted independently by Goal, so both the time and the channel can be treated as firm. Worth flagging that USA Network is the good outcome here - four of the other five 10am kick-offs that morning are Peacock-only. ODDS ARE STILL NOT RECORDED, and this is a deliberate omission rather than an oversight. Every mainstream book and odds-comparison site refused the request on 8 September: FanDuel, DraftKings, Oddschecker, Oddspedia, Forebet, BetUS and YesPlay all returned 403. The only two numbers that surfaced came through search summaries that could not be opened and verified - YesPlay quoting 1.23 on Chelsea, 6.60 the draw and 11.00 on Hull, and Polymarket, a prediction market rather than a sportsbook, trading Chelsea 79 cents, the draw 15 and Hull 7. Those two agree closely once normalised, at roughly 77-79 percent Chelsea, 14-15 percent draw and 7-9 percent Hull, so the shape of the market is clear enough: a heavy home favourite, materially shorter than the Leeds cup price. But neither source is a mainstream sportsbook and neither could be read first-hand, so nothing has been written into the odds fields. This should be picked up on the next run, when the briefing text falls due. TEAM NEWS SO FAR, which is thin because the Leeds cup tie on 9 September is soaking up all the reporting: Moises Caicedo is being openly targeted at this match rather than the cup tie. He has not played since lasting 14 minutes against Brighton, and Alonso has said the injury is not longer-term but that he will not repeat the mistake of rushing him back, so Hull is the stated return date rather than Wednesday. Marco Palestra is also pointed at this game, having missed all four matches so far with a training-ground knock. Jordan Henderson is still waiting on his Chelsea debut with the wrist injury he carried out of the World Cup - he was pictured in first-team training on 4 September and Alonso is waiting on a green light, so mid-to-late September looks more realistic than this weekend. NO PROJECTED XI YET, on purpose. Nothing current exists: the only Chelsea-versus-Hull predicted lineup in circulation is dated 13 February 2026 and is for an FA Cup tie at the MKM Stadium under a different manager, with several players in it who are now unavailable or gone. It was discarded. Any XI for this match is also hostage to how heavily Alonso rotates on Wednesday, so a projection is worth more after the cup tie than before it.
